reading.body:
CyrusOne's OCB1 in Council Bluffs, Iowa, is a 9 MW data center, half of Iowa's disclosed 18 MW across two facilities, and cannot support hyperscale AI training clusters.

The 9 MW IT load supports roughly 225 racks at 40 kW per rack, or under 100 accelerators after non-compute overhead. Its 420,000 square feet of technical space is large for that power level, indicating a multi-hall regional campus built for general colocation rather than dense compute.

The certifications, PCI DSS, HIPAA, FISMA, HITRUST, and TIA-942, point to regulated enterprise workloads, not AI research. Within Iowa, OCB1 is one of only two facilities with published capacity and holds half of the state's declared 18 MW, while 52 mapped sites publish no power figures, making disclosed capacity rare.

The data does not identify tenants, actual rack density, or any AI deployments. A suitability score of 56, with announced expansion missing, reflects limited published inputs and no signal of growth, so this campus is a regional asset, not a node in a hyperscaler's power-constrained buildout.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
